Market research firm Counterpoint Research's latest report shows that Apple surpassed Samsung in Europe's carrier sales channel in Q2 2026, becoming the leading smartphone brand in the region, thanks to its carrier channel sales outperforming the overall market. Details are as follows.

Apple drives European carrier channel sales, outperforming the overall smartphone market

Counterpoint Research's report published today indicates that smartphones sold through European carriers in Q2 2026 fell 4% year-on-year, compared with an 11% decline in the open market. The report shows that overall smartphone sales fell 8% year-on-year.

Counterpoint said this situation once again reflects the impact of rising memory costs, with the European low-end smartphone market being hit particularly hard. The relatively better performance of the carrier channel is because their customer base tends to purchase high-end devices on contract, as well as products from high-end brands such as Apple.

The report pointed out that Apple's share of European carrier smartphone sales rose from 33% in Q2 2025 to 37% in Q2 2026; over the same period, Samsung fell from 39% to 34%.

However, in terms of year-on-year growth, Chinese brand vivo recorded the largest increase in carrier channel sales, reaching 90%; Motorola came in a distant second with 27% growth.

The following is a response from Counterpoint Research Associate Director Jan Stryjak on the relevant data:

Stryjak added that he expects the carrier channel to continue expanding its market share in the coming quarters, as the low-end market will continue to be affected by the "memory crisis". He also pointed out that independent retailers have stepped up their promotional efforts, a move that "may relieve some of the pricing pressure with carriers and provide additional stimulus to the open market".
